parts.name: Left frontal lobe
parts.info: Plans, decides and controls movement. The precentral gyrus at its back edge is the primary motor cortex.
parts.fact: Broca's area, which produces speech, sits in the left inferior frontal gyrus in most people.

parts.name: Right frontal lobe
parts.info: Plans, decides and controls movement. The precentral gyrus at its back edge is the primary motor cortex.
parts.fact: Broca's area, which produces speech, sits in the left inferior frontal gyrus in most people.

parts.name: Left parietal lobe
parts.info: Combines touch, body position and space. The postcentral gyrus is the primary area for touch.
parts.fact: Damage to the right parietal lobe can make a person ignore the left side of space.

parts.name: Right parietal lobe
parts.info: Combines touch, body position and space. The postcentral gyrus is the primary area for touch.
parts.fact: Damage to the right parietal lobe can make a person ignore the left side of space.

parts.name: Left temporal lobe
parts.info: Hearing, language understanding and recognising faces and objects.
parts.fact: Wernicke's area, needed to understand speech, lies at the back of the left superior temporal gyrus.

parts.name: Right temporal lobe
parts.info: Hearing, language understanding and recognising faces and objects.
parts.fact: Wernicke's area, needed to understand speech, lies at the back of the left superior temporal gyrus.

parts.name: Left occipital lobe
parts.info: The main visual centre. It turns signals from the eyes into what you see.
parts.fact: Each occipital lobe sees the opposite half of the visual field.

parts.name: Right occipital lobe
parts.info: The main visual centre. It turns signals from the eyes into what you see.
parts.fact: Each occipital lobe sees the opposite half of the visual field.

parts.name: Left limbic cortex
parts.info: The cingulate and parahippocampal gyri, on the inner face of the hemisphere, link emotion, attention and memory.
parts.fact: The cingulate gyrus wraps around the corpus callosum like a belt, which is what 'cingulate' means.

parts.name: Right limbic cortex
parts.info: The cingulate and parahippocampal gyri, on the inner face of the hemisphere, link emotion, attention and memory.
parts.fact: The cingulate gyrus wraps around the corpus callosum like a belt, which is what 'cingulate' means.

parts.name: Left insula
parts.info: A hidden lobe folded deep inside the lateral sulcus. It senses the body's inner state: taste, pain, heartbeat and disgust.
parts.fact: You only see the insula once the overlying frontal and temporal lobes are hidden or sliced.

parts.name: Right insula
parts.info: A hidden lobe folded deep inside the lateral sulcus. It senses the body's inner state: taste, pain, heartbeat and disgust.
parts.fact: You only see the insula once the overlying frontal and temporal lobes are hidden or sliced.

parts.name: Left cerebral white matter
parts.info: Bundles of insulated nerve fibres that connect cortex areas to each other and to the rest of the nervous system.
parts.fact: White matter looks white because of myelin, the fatty insulation around nerve fibres.

parts.name: Right cerebral white matter
parts.info: Bundles of insulated nerve fibres that connect cortex areas to each other and to the rest of the nervous system.
parts.fact: White matter looks white because of myelin, the fatty insulation around nerve fibres.

parts.name: Basal ganglia
parts.info: The caudate nucleus, putamen and globus pallidus. They help start wanted movements and suppress unwanted ones.
parts.fact: Parkinson's disease affects the circuits that run through the basal ganglia.

parts.name: Thalamus
parts.info: Two egg-shaped relay centres. Almost every sense except smell passes through the thalamus on its way to the cortex. Includes the pineal gland.
parts.fact: The lateral geniculate body, part of the thalamus, relays vision from the eyes to the occipital lobe.

parts.name: Hippocampus & amygdala
parts.info: The hippocampus turns new experiences into long-term memories. The almond-shaped amygdala processes fear and emotion.
parts.fact: The hippocampus is named after the seahorse, which its curved shape resembles.

parts.name: Corpus callosum & fornix
parts.info: The corpus callosum is a broad bridge of about 200 million fibres joining the two hemispheres. The fornix carries signals out of the hippocampus.
parts.fact: It is the largest white-matter structure in the brain.

parts.name: Hypothalamus & pituitary
parts.info: Controls body temperature, hunger, thirst and sleep, and steers the pituitary, the master hormone gland hanging below it.
parts.fact: The hypothalamus is about the size of an almond yet controls most of the body's hormones.

parts.name: Optic chiasm & tracts
parts.info: Where the optic nerves meet and half of each nerve's fibres cross to the other side, so each hemisphere sees the opposite half of the world.
parts.fact: A pituitary tumour pressing on the chiasm can cause loss of the outer half of vision in both eyes.

parts.name: Ventricles
parts.info: Connected cavities filled with cerebrospinal fluid, shown in blue. The fluid cushions the brain and carries away waste.
parts.fact: The body makes about 500 ml of cerebrospinal fluid a day and replaces it three to four times.

parts.name: Midbrain
parts.info: The top of the brainstem. Controls eye movements and reflexes to sudden sights and sounds.
parts.fact: The superior and inferior colliculi on its back make you turn toward a flash or a bang.

parts.name: Pons
parts.info: A bulge in the brainstem that relays signals between the cortex and the cerebellum and helps control breathing and sleep.
parts.fact: 'Pons' is Latin for bridge.

parts.name: Medulla oblongata
parts.info: Connects the brain to the spinal cord. Runs automatic functions such as heart rate, blood pressure and breathing.
parts.fact: Most motor fibres cross from one side to the other here, which is why each half of the brain controls the opposite side of the body.

parts.name: Cerebellum
parts.info: Fine-tunes movement, balance and posture, and helps learn motor skills like riding a bike.
parts.fact: It holds more than half of all the brain's neurons.
